html:
Stephen I was the first king of Hungary, crowned on Christmas Day 1000 or New Year's Day 1001, who turned the Magyar principality into a Christian kingdom and ruled until his death in 1038.

Born Vajk in Esztergom, son of the grand prince Géza, he was baptised and married Gisela of Bavaria. He crushed pagan rivals, set up bishoprics and monasteries, and organised the land into counties under royal castles. His crown, said to be a gift of the Pope, became the symbol of the Hungarian state. His laws and advice to his son shaped the kingdom founded after the Magyar settlement. He was made a saint in 1083, and his feast on 20 August is Hungary's national day. The Kingdom of Hungary lasted until 1946, and his right hand is kept as a relic in Budapest.
sum: Stephen I was the first king of Hungary, crowned on Christmas Day 1000 or New Year's Day 1001, who turned the Magyar principality into a Christian kingdom and ruled until his death in 1038.
